title: KV tiling reservoir: batch-aware allocation and fragmentation mitigation playbook
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Problem: As continuous batching volume increases across variable-length chat workloads, per-GPU KV cache pools show rising internal fragmentation and uneven slot utilization. This causes higher OOM throttles for hot workloads and suboptimal batching efficiency for medium-length sequences. Existing slab compaction jobs are heavy-weight (full-pass) and cause GC pauses that violate latency SLOs.

Goal: Introduce a low-latency, batch-aware allocation strategy (tiling reservoir) plus lightweight micro-compaction and slot remapping to reduce fragmentation without impacting token tail-latency. The playbook below outlines design, telemetry, rollout, and acceptance criteria. The approach favors opportunistic, incremental fixes rather than global stop-the-world compactions so production path remains smooth for Dedicated and Hosted clusters.
motivation_and_context: Continuous batching increases throughput but amplifies variance in per-request KV footprint. Small, popular prefixes create hot islands while long-running chat sessions pin large KV spans. Without smarter allocation and fast micro-healing we waste contiguous GPU memory and increase cache miss pressure. This work aligns with recent autoscaling and batching changes (see runtime-1.20 batching PRs) and is a prerequisite for more aggressive quantization and pack-aligned kernels.
proposal_summary:
1) Introduce a tiled reservoir allocator that divides KV pool into fixed micro-tiles (configurable tile_size) and allocates tiles instead of arbitrary byte ranges to reduce hole creation.
2) Make allocation batch-aware: prefer co-locating tiles for requests in the same batch to maintain locality and enable prefix reuse.
3) Implement lightweight micro-compaction: background thread merges adjacent free tiles and performs selective remap of cold tiles to consolidate hot ranges. Micro-compaction uses bounded CPU/GPU cycles and is throttled to SLO-safe budgets.
4) Add a fast, lock-free slot reclamation probe to detect stale KV handles (per-conversation TTL) and opportunistically free their tiles during low-util windows.
5) Telemetry: emit slot-level churn, fragmentation ratio, average tile lifetime, micro-compaction time, and allocation tail-latency.
6) Rollout via canary on Dedicated pools then opt-in Hosted clusters with runtime toggle and kill-switch.
implementation_plan: Add tiled-reservoir allocator module with configurable tile_size and reservoir_count.
Integrate batch context to allocator API: allocator.allocate_for_batch(batch_id, est_kv_bytes).
Implement micro-compaction worker with rate limiter and compaction budget per-GPU.
Add TTL-based probe and reclamation path to free orphaned tiles.
Expose new telemetry metrics and Grafana dashboards.
Write e2e test harness using replayed production traces with varied sequence lengths.
Create runtime feature flag and kill-switch for immediate rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation ratio (free contiguous bytes / total free bytes) improves by >= 40% on replayed mixed workloads compared to baseline.
Tail P95 token latency increase < 1% with micro-compaction enabled under steady-state load.
OOM throttle events reduce by >= 30% for high-concurrency chat workloads in Dedicated canary pool.
Telemetry dashboards populated and alerting rules for compaction budget exceedance configured.
PRs merged and runtime flag added with rollout docs and rollback steps.
tasks: Unit + integration tests using trace-replay harness (Unit Test Team)
Grafana dashboard and SLO updates (Observability Team)
Canary rollout on Dedicated, monitor for regressions (SRE)
Performance signoff meeting and release notes (PM)
Post-rollout 2-week regression sweep and metrics review (PM & Eng)
Security review (if any sensitive mapping used) (Security)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Remapping cold tiles may briefly increase memory pressure. Mitigation: micro-compaction is budgeted and verifies free-target before remap.
Risk: Batch-aware allocation could worsen placement for heterogenous batch mixes. Mitigation: allocator falls back to best-fit outside strong batch-locality signals.
Risk: Telemetry noise from short-lived allocations. Mitigation: use exponentially smoothed metrics and minimum lifetime thresholds.
Risk: Hard-to-reproduce fragmentation patterns in canary. Mitigation: run trace-replay harness with stratified sampling of tenants.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): unit tests + trace replay; validate improvement on canary traces.
Stage 2 (canary Dedicated): enable flag for 5% of Dedicated capacity for 48h; monitor telemetry and SLOs.
Stage 3 (broader Dedicated): ramp to 50% over 1 week if stable.
Stage 4 (Hosted opt-in): expose flag in Console for customers to opt into tiling reservoir; monitor environmental differences.
Rollback: feature flag off; run immediate micro-compaction abort and restore previous allocator state from snapshot.
notes: This approach intentionally avoids full-heap compactions. The micro-compaction worker is designed to be incremental and preemptible.
Tile size trade-off: smaller tiles reduce internal waste but increase metadata overhead; we'll expose tile_size knob and test [256B, 1KB, 4KB] in replay harness.
Coordination: align with batching autotuner changes scheduled in runtime-1.22 so we don't regress packing heuristics.
